question.problem:
Given that 
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3} & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],$
evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$

Given that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131042/assets/557cc8f0b4fd805df7fb5a7f9dd3d9abf803847582cb71c8106959103b2f5b91.svg) 
 evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(0,1).$
current_example.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131042/assets/8b53a15dca924d0be9d912a9c11a9b986c14dcf79c68f836718a3a0881513c50.svg)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131042/assets/040c39e24d35744acb3d16258a96fbc401dd204ce462fe198797d636730ec1c9.svg)

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det \left( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \right)
$$

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131042/assets/7730162de09bea3b2ff3cb6d7e006cd31c40e5a39111e9677b6ddb9b17d6353a.svg)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131042/assets/7ecd9f0c283b8b669f1ed9c032a83eddb483ddc2dfaa93de00e5c152fa16a704.svg) we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = \ln y, 
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1) = 0 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 1 = -1.
$$
